title: Rectangular base
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector of [0.0, 0.0, 0.0374] to position the origin slightly above the global origin. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a new face. In this first face, draw a closed loop consisting of four lines: the first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0); the second line starts at (0.75, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0187); the third line starts at (0.75, 0.0187) and ends at (0.0, 0.0187); and the fourth line completes the loop by starting at (0.0, 0.0187) and ending at the origin. After drawing the loop, apply a sketch scale of 0.75 to reduce the size proportionally. Rotate the scaled sketch using Euler angles of [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translate it using the vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0374] to align it correctly. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.0374 units in the direction opposite to the normal, ensuring that the extrusion forms a new solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular base will be 0.75 units in length, 0.0187 units in width, and 0.0374 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Translate the coordinate system
workplane = workplane.translate((0.0, 0.0, 0.0374))

# Create the sketch
sketch = (
    workplane
    .lineTo(0.75, 0.0)  # line_1
    .lineTo(0.75, 0.0187)  # line_2
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0187)  # line_3
    .lineTo(0.0, 0.0)  # line_4
    .close()  # Close the loop
)

# Extrude the sketch
extrusion = sketch.extrude(0.0374)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = extrusion

# Display the final model
